designs.title: No.
designs.why: Strong, simple lockup: the cat lying across the top rule of a heavy NO, with its paw pinning the ball that doubles as the full stop, makes a clear one-ink joke that reads from 3 m on both tees. The inked line work is confident and the cat's sour face does the talking. Typographically it is shakier. The tail uses the same white-slash hatching as the letters and runs straight into the N's left stem, so at a distance it reads as a stray striped stroke before the N and the word's left edge goes mushy. The stripes inside the letters are cut evenly and look mechanical, which fights the loose brush line of the cat. The stop sits a little too far from the O and is half hidden by the paw, so it reads as a ball first and a full stop second. The bottom rule also stops short of the left edge of the N. On the tee the whole mark is small and sits high for a back print.
designs.fix: Pull the tail clear of the N with a clean gap of white (or redraw it in solid line or a different hatch angle from the letter stripes) so NO reads as a clean word with the cat as its frame. At the same time, nudge the ball in to normal full-stop spacing on the baseline.
